A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DLF/DRGD research, with readable main texts, equations, figures and appendices. The retained appendices can be matched despite renumbering and the addition of Appendix A in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original optimization experiments on orthogonal groups and reference-tracking simulations for a double pendulum and unicycle car, including supplementary trajectories in Appendix G.

after.justification: V2 retains these original numerical experiments and their outcomes in Section 6 and Appendix H.

M1.justification: DLF and DRGD retain the same updates in Equations (8) and (12), score training and network architectures. Renaming the approximate projection from s to v clarifies notation. The link-function sign correction does not change the implemented operators already specified in v1.

E1.justification: Both evaluate O(10), O(20), double-pendulum tracking and unicycle tracking, including the same additional reference trajectories. Newly mentioned design applications and related reinforcement-learning work are contextual examples, not added evaluations.

E2.justification: The empirical comparisons retain exact landing, exact objective minima and training-set minima where previously shown. V2 discusses graph-based, latent-space and pull-back approaches but does not evaluate them as additional baselines.

E3.justification: Section 6 and the matched experimental appendices retain the same sample counts, noise settings, horizon of 100, training budgets, discretization and optimization step sizes. The control iteration budgets and true-system back-testing procedure are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the noise-level comparison on O(n), checks of optimized trajectories against true-system outputs, and the additional unicycle reference examples. No new ablation, robustness test or empirical supplementary analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for these experiments. V2 introduces no statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All matched plot images are identical, including the orthogonal-group curves, tracking trajectories and objective histories. The reported findings are retained; v1 Figure 3 becoming v2 Figure 2 is relocation rather than a result change.

T1.justification: Equation (3) changes the link function's log-density term from negative to positive, making it consistent with Equation (4). New Appendix A adds supplementary mathematical connections to denoising autoencoders, a stationarity-equivalence argument for latent parametrizations, and recovery of the classical O(N^-1/2) gradient-norm rate. The main approximation and convergence theorems remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction and contribution summary narrow the priority claim from the first algorithms/framework for optimization over data manifolds to the first score-based framework. V2 also drops the claim of providing the first non-asymptotic convergence analysis. The substantive projection-recovery and convergence claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds substantial comparative interpretation: it explains the lower-dimensional extension of denoising-autoencoder results and contrasts projection learning with latent charts through intrinsic-dimension requirements, chart validity, architectural constraints and pull-back computation costs. These applicability and mechanism discussions were absent from v1. Existing empirical interpretations and the strong uniform-approximation limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V1 Appendix G and v2 Appendix H disclose the same data-generation procedures, MLP and one-dimensional UNet architectures, Adam settings, learning-rate schedules, epochs, RK4 discretization and optimization parameters. V2 adds no code/data access information or resource measurements.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 and new Appendix A substantially expand positioning against graph-based manifold denoising, GANs and autoencoders, manifold flows, latent-space optimization and natural gradients. Specific additions include Wang et al. (2025), Alain and Bengio (2014), and Amari (1998). This accompanies the narrower score-based novelty claim.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introductory explanation and contribution summary, restructures manifold-learning discussion into parametric and non-parametric approaches, and adds a dedicated comparisons appendix. It also clarifies score-versus-denoiser terminology throughout, streamlines the preliminaries and adds acknowledgments.

P2.justification: The orthogonal-group plot moves from Appendix G to the main text and gains a caption explaining exact landing. Other figures are repositioned or renumbered, and the author block is reformatted. The plots themselves are unchanged, with no new figures or tables.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects the central link-function sign inconsistency, clarifies notation and replaces an overly broad priority claim with better contextualized score-based positioning. These provide a limited overall gain while retaining the original evidence and guarantees. However, new Appendix A.2 Equation (18) uses the metric G rather than its inverse despite claiming pull-back Riemannian equivalence; this localized mathematical error limits the benefit of the added comparisons.
